terms.definition: A support-staff member who studies film or data for a team; titles include recruiting analyst (college) and data analyst (NFL).
A scout who covers a specific geographic area of the country or specific conferences, visiting schools and writing reports on prospects.
A deputy to the general manager; the NFL media policy treats the title as a 'secondary football executive' who is next in line to the top football executive and supervises player personnel.
All the coaches who work under a head coach; the typical NFL team has about 15 assistants, and a college team about 9 full-time assistants plus 2 graduate assistants.
A scout who adds extra looks, or exposures, at a prospect beyond the area scout's reports; ESPN equates the role with a national scout.
The assistant coach responsible for a team's defense, usually the game-plan builder and play-caller, who oversees the defensive position coaches.
The assistant who works exclusively with the defensive linemen on technique such as run stopping, gap control and pass rush.
The scouting executive who organizes a team's draft board, grading college players, directing the area scouts and checking background.

The executive who leads a team's player personnel department; in the NFL (Bleacher Report) he mainly handles players already in the league, while college DPPs run recruiting, roster management and portal work.
terms.variants: director of pro personnel (Bleacher Report usage)

terms.definition: The front-office executive who handles players already in the NFL: contract talks with free agents and extensions, and evaluation of other teams' rosters.
terms.variants: director of pro scouting (draft title, not found)

terms.definition: A staff executive who leads a college program's recruiting department.
The staff member who runs a team's equipment room.
The department of a college football program that handles non-coaching support such as logistics; major programs typically staff 4-10 people in it (an SMWW estimate).
A college staff executive who runs recruiting, roster building, transfer-portal work and support staff, so the head coach can focus on coaching.
The NFL executive who oversees a club's roster and contracts and answers directly to the owner (or chairman); he builds the personnel staff and hires the head coach.
terms.variants: vice president of football operations (alternate title, Bleacher Report)

terms.definition: A junior college coaching or support staffer; a typical college team has about two alongside nine full-time assistants.
The coach at the top of a team's coaching structure, above the coordinators.
The assistant who coaches linebackers on tackling, pass-rushing and coverage drops, ranking just below the defensive coordinator on many staffs.
A scout who adds extra looks at top prospects across the country; ESPN says teams call this an 'over the top' scout or cross-checker.
The assistant coach responsible for a team's offense, usually the game-plan builder and play-caller, who oversees the offensive position coaches.
The assistant who trains the offensive linemen and works with the coordinator on the running game; he sometimes also holds a run-game title.
The person or family that owns the franchise; top football executives such as the general manager report to the owner or chairman.
An assistant coach in charge of one position group, such as quarterbacks or defensive line.
The club executive over the business side: finances, marketing, ticket prices and similar; some teams combine president and CEO.
A scout who evaluates players on other teams' rosters, used for trades and free agency.
An entry-level coach who analyzes game film for statistical breakdowns to prepare the team for upcoming opponents.
terms.variants: offensive, defensive and special teams quality control

terms.definition: An assistant who works with the quarterback's footwork, drop and throwing motion and watches his mental and physical habits.
The assistant coach a program tabs to run its recruiting; at major programs this work has moved to larger recruiting departments.

An NFL policy requiring clubs to interview at least two external candidates who are persons of color and/or women for head coach, GM and coordinator openings (and one for quarterback coach and senior executive jobs).
The head of a club's scouting department, who reviews the area scouts' weekly reports and sets prospect grades.
The assistant who coaches the defensive backs (cornerbacks and safeties) on pass coverage.
The assistant coach in charge of the kicking game: kickers, punters, long snappers, returners and the coverage and return units.
terms.variants: merged draft rows: special teams coordinator (two copies)

terms.definition: The coach who runs a team's weight training and conditioning, and works with doctors on rehab.
The club doctor responsible for players' medical care; in the NFL concussion protocol the team physician evaluates the player on the sideline together with the unaffiliated neurotrauma consultant.
The staffer who runs a team's film and video operations.
